howTo.title: Open a business (any type)
howTo.steps: Before signing a lease, talk to the Economic Development Office, confirm zoning allows your use, and request a free informal walk-through with Inspection and Fire staff. After choosing a site, get any land use approvals (Historic District Commission, Planning Board or conditional use permits), then apply for a building permit in the permit portal and choose Tenant Fit-Up, which applies to every new business even if nothing changes. A Certificate of Occupancy is issued after inspections.

source.label: City of Portsmouth, How to Start a Business

howTo.title: Open a restaurant or food business
howTo.steps: Contact the Health Department early; a free walk-through is usually scheduled within two business days and food service floor plans must be approved before construction. Use the New/Renovated Food Establishment Checklist and the Restaurant Construction Guide, then apply in the OpenGov/ViewPoint portal. The permit is issued after pre-opening inspections; annual permits expire September 30 and seasonal permits October 15.

howTo.title: Outdoor dining (sidewalk, parking space or travel lane cafe)
howTo.steps: Apply through the city permit portal for an Outdoor Dining Encumbrance Permit; the 2026 application period opened March 10, with public realm use from May 1 to October 12. Fees are $5 per square foot of cafe area with a $750 minimum for sidewalks, parking spaces or travel lanes. If the cafe extends in front of a neighboring business, get that abutter's written consent first. Planning Department: (603) 610-7216.

source.label: City of Portsmouth, Outdoor Dining Encumbrance Permits 2026

howTo.title: Sidewalk obstruction license (tables, chairs, A-frame signs, racks)
howTo.steps: Any table, chair, bench, A-frame sign, clothing rack or mannequin on a city sidewalk needs a sidewalk obstruction license. Review Chapter 6, Article I of the city ordinances, then apply or renew through the Permitting and Licensing portal. City Clerk: (603) 610-7245.

source.label: City of Portsmouth, Sidewalk Obstruction License

howTo.title: Vendor or peddler license
howTo.steps: Anyone selling goods or food while moving from place to place on city property needs a Vending (Hawkers and Peddlers) License from the City Clerk. Food vendors must first get a license from the Health Department. Complete the 2026 vendor application and bring it to the City Clerk at 1 Junkins Avenue.

howTo.title: Sign permit
howTo.steps: Sign regulations are Article 12 of the Zoning Ordinance. The Inspection Department does not issue sign permits; contact the Planning Department at 603-610-7216. Signs in the historic district may also need Historic District Commission review.

howTo.title: Business license
howTo.steps: The City of Portsmouth does not require a general business license. The State of New Hampshire issues business registrations through the Secretary of State (603-271-3242).

notices.title: Opportunity Zone 2.0 designations approved for 25 NH census tracts
notices.detail: Governor Ayotte announced U.S. Treasury approval of 25 New Hampshire tracts across all 10 counties, effective January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2036. The article does not name Portsmouth tracts; maps are on the state website.

notices.title: Free legal, accounting and financial consulting for small businesses via NH SBDC
notices.detail: Devine Millimet partnered with the NH Small Business Development Center to offer up to five hours of private sessions with legal, accounting or financial professionals through the SBDC LeAF program.

notices.title: FY27 CDBG public facility and accessibility grants open
notices.detail: Grants of roughly $25,000 to $150,000 for 501(c)(3) nonprofits serving low and moderate income Portsmouth residents or making ADA improvements. Rolling applications until December 18, 2026; shovel-ready projects finishing by February 20, 2027 get priority. Contact Kay Wright, 603-610-7281.

notices.title: Cate Street Bridge project public information session
notices.detail: DPW held a public session on October 20 at the Senior Activity Center with project updates and Q&A on the Cate Street Bridge construction.

notices.title: Parking restrictions and road closures for the October 31 Halloween Parade
notices.detail: The parade will cause significant traffic delays along its downtown route; drivers are urged to use alternate roads and parking restrictions apply along the route.

notices.title: 2026 outdoor dining season ended October 12
notices.detail: Per the city's March 10 notice, use of sidewalks, travel lanes and parking spaces for outdoor dining ran May 1 through October 12, 2026. Applications for the next season are handled by the Planning Department.

notices.title: City evaluates stormwater funding options, including a possible stormwater utility
notices.detail: The city hired Raftelis Financial Consultants to study whether to create a dedicated Stormwater Enterprise Utility, which could change how stormwater infrastructure is funded and billed to property owners.

notices.title: Council parking work session: proposed short-term rate increase and workforce parking options
notices.detail: Staff proposed on-street and lot rates of $3 per hour for the first 3 hours and $6 per hour after. Downtown workforce options include the Parrott Avenue pilot (about $3.35 for a 10-hour day, 108 spaces) and the Foundry Garage ($3 for up to 10 hours, up to 20 times a month). Foundry workforce parking hit 160 cars a day in July 2026.

source.label: City of Portsmouth, City Council parking work session presentation

programs.name: Economic Revitalization Zone (ERZ) tax credits
programs.what: State tax credits against the Business Profits Tax and Business Enterprise Tax, up to $40,000 a year for five years, for businesses that expand or relocate and create full-time jobs in one of five Portsmouth zones: Pease Tradeport, Portsmouth Office Park (Commerce Way), Heritage-Constitution Industrial Park, Central Business District and West End.

programs.name: Outdoor Dining Encumbrance Permit
programs.what: Seasonal permit to use sidewalks, parking spaces or travel lanes for cafe seating, May 1 to October 12 in 2026, at $5 per square foot with a $750 minimum.

programs.name: Downtown Workforce Parking Program
programs.what: Discounted parking for downtown employees: Foundry Garage at $3 for up to 10 hours (up to 20 times a month) and the Parrott Avenue on-street pilot at 30 cents an hour plus a 35 cent fee.

source.label: City of Portsmouth, parking work session Aug 17, 2026

programs.name: FY27 CDBG Public Facility and Accessibility Improvement Grants
programs.what: Competitive grants, generally $25,000 to $150,000, for 501(c)(3) nonprofits; applications accepted on a rolling basis until December 18, 2026.

programs.name: SBDC counseling and SCORE mentoring
programs.what: Free one-on-one business counseling through the NH SBDC and free mentoring and workshops through Seacoast SCORE; the Portsmouth Public Library also offers business research databases.

programs.name: Foreign Trade Zone No. 81
programs.what: Three Portsmouth sites (Pease International Tradeport, the Port of New Hampshire and the Portsmouth Industrial Park on Lafayette Road) are part of Foreign Trade Zone 81, awarded in 1982.

programs.name: Small business loans (BFA, GSDC, Community Loan Fund, ICCD microloans, SBA 7(a))
programs.what: Loan and guaranty programs listed by the city for fixed assets, equipment, working capital and microloans up to $25,000.
